Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Purge / invalidation bus and access-log pipeline (Kafka)

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 120,000 rps at the edge: 80% cacheable static assets, 15% dynamic/API pass-through, 4% video segments, 1% purge and log-shipping traffic.

assumptions.subject: edge
assumptions.statement: 94% L1 hit ratio at the PoP for static assets; 80% of the remaining misses are absorbed by the regional shield, so only 1.2% of static requests reach the origin object store. Video segments cache better still (90% L1).

assumptions.subject: dns
assumptions.statement: GeoDNS is visited on ~2% of requests - resolver and browser DNS caches absorb the rest. A DNS tier sized off raw request rate would be ~50x over-provisioned.

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Dynamic requests get a 15% edge micro-cache hit, then a 90% hit on the origin fragment cache, so only 8.5% of dynamic requests (1.3% of all traffic) reach Postgres.

assumptions.subject: edge
assumptions.statement: COST WARNING - read this before quoting the total. The edge PoPs and the shield are a MANAGED CDN: they have no per-instance price in Keystone's grounded catalogue (CloudFront bills per GB and per request, per distribution), so their compute line is $0. Bandwidth IS modelled: 9,331,200 GB/month = 120k rps x 30 KB average response, priced at the $0.09/GB LIST rate. That single line dominates every other cost in this design by two orders of magnitude, which is the true shape of CDN economics.

assumptions.subject: edge
assumptions.statement: The $0.09/GB list rate is what a small account pays. At ~9 PB/month nobody pays list: committed-use CDN contracts at this volume run roughly 5-20x cheaper. Treat the bandwidth figure as an UPPER BOUND, and the real number as a negotiation, not a calculation.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: The v1 engine is single-region. A CDN is inherently multi-region: `edge` at instances=9 stands in for 9 PoPs and `shield` for 3 regional tiers, but the engine treats them as one load-balanced pool with one latency, so it cannot express geographic RTT, per-region hit ratios, or a regional PoP failure shifting load to its neighbours.

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: The binding constraint here is the ORIGIN application tier, not the edge - and that is the lesson of the design. Across ALL traffic the CDN absorbs 86% of requests; the other 14% (12.75% dynamic pass-through plus 1.2% static/video origin fills) still reach origin. Static assets alone are absorbed at 98.8% - do not quote that figure for the whole system. The requests that survive to origin are the expensive dynamic ones, so origin capacity is what you actually size. Edge PoP count is the CDN vendor's problem, not a dial you turn.

_library.summary: Two-tier edge cache (PoP plus regional shield) that serves static and video traffic near users and shields a dynamic origin.
